patches.why: Runtime external SetVariable(FLAG correct_code) (case in the setter dispatch 0x180018260, registered by setup_bindings as binding +0x80): setne cl -> mov cl,1. Whatever the level's keypad logic writes when a code is checked, correct_code becomes true through the normal setter, so the engine's change notification fires and the keypad's own branch and the door scripts (delegate_OnChanged on keypad.correct_code) all see the same true value. The identical level-load initializer at 0x18001923f (binding +0x70 -> 0x180004b50) is left alone so keypads don't start unlocked.

evidence: Script 1b9174546ee05f8a.dll is the keypad's panel/display script (nodes: SetText2/SetColorUI/SetAlphaUI, PlaySound, Delay, Blackboard flag/string/exists expressions; no input handling). Flags: +0xb2 correct_code, +0xb4 UPDATING, +0xb5 Disabled (getter dispatch 0x180017a10). Nothing in any script writes correct_code; it is written only through the bindings, i.e. by the level's keypad logic after the code check. Door scripts ce88d9fe9bdf02d4 / cfadc41efdf8e856 / ee79d2b57e157978 only read keypad.correct_code via ExternalScriptFlagExpression and react with delegate_onset / delegate_OnChanged. Names resolved with echo-symbols data/names.tsv.
risk: Previous version (3 patches forcing every read of correct_code to 1 and the panel's branch to exec_true) softlocked: a wrong code sent the panel into its success/disabled state while the stored value never changed, so the doors' OnChanged never fired and nothing opened (reported 2026-11-10). This version only changes what gets stored, so all readers stay consistent. NOT verified in game: if the level writes correct_code only for a right code, a wrong code still fails and resets like vanilla (no softlock, but the switch does nothing); if it writes on every digit, the door may open before all four digits are in.
